title: Selective erase index + query-gate for auditable analytics deletion
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Build a two-layer deletion system for usage analytics: (1) a durable, auditable "erase ledger" and selective-erase index that records erase intents and maps to event shards; (2) a lightweight Query Gate component that enforces deletion policies at query-time for downstream analytics consumers while a background compactor performs safe physical removal. Goal is provable deletion, low blast radius on queries, and exportable attestation for customers and compliance teams.
technical_design: Architecture: (A) Erase Controller service receives deletion requests (customer/tenant id, selectors, retention-window) and writes an immutable erase manifest into the 'analytics-erase-ledger' bucket (append-only, versioned). (B) Manifest is structured as list of selectors + opaque deletion token + lower/upper timestamp bounds. (C) A Selective-Erase Index (SI) is built by the streaming consumer: index maps coarse shard keys (date, dataset, customer-hash, event-fingerprint) to erase-token(s). Index stored in low-latency KV store (CockroachDB readonly replicas) and periodically compacted. (D) Query Gate: lightweight middleware in the analytics query path (ClickHouse/Clickhouse-read-alike or OLAP cache) that applies index lookups to filter or redact rows at query time for interactive dashboards and scheduled exports. (E) Compactor Worker: background job that, after configurable safety window and attestations, performs physical row deletion in downstream stores (deletes in ClickHouse, tombstone compaction in event-store S3). (F) Audit & Attestation: Controller signs a deletion attestation (SHA256 manifest + timestamp + operator id) and stores in audit-log (immutable). Customers can request attestation bundles for legal/regulatory compliance.
acceptance_criteria: A deletion request can be created through the Console and produces an immutable erase manifest in the ledger
Query Gate blocks or redacts rows matching the delete selectors for interactive dashboards within 1 minute of manifest creation for >95% of queries (p95)
Compactor job permanently removes rows in demo dataset within the safety window and records compaction event into audit-log
Audit attestation bundle can be exported (manifest + compaction receipts + signature) for a given request id
End-to-end test demonstrates idempotency: re-submitting the same delete request does not change index state or duplicate compaction actions
Security review sign-off on manifest encryption-at-rest and HSM-backed signing process
migrations: Create analytics-erase-ledger S3 bucket with object lock and versioning; IAM-only write for erase-controller service
Add Selective-Erase Index schema to the privacy_kv cluster (table: erase_index) and backfill using 14-day sliding window consumer for 90 days of history
Deploy Query Gate as sidecar in analytics-read API and route 100% of Console interactive queries through it behind feature flag
risks: Query-time filtering introduces latency; mitigated by coarse-grained index sharding and LRU cache on queries
Index eventual consistency may allow short window of leakage for long-running analytic queries; safety window and conservative default selectors to reduce footprint
Compaction in ClickHouse can be expensive; will throttle compactor and run during off-peak with adaptive batch sizes
Customer attestation requires secure key management; need HSM/KMS integration and rotate signing keys with retention of old keys for verification
test_plan: Unit tests for erase-controller manifest generation and schema validation
Integration test: create delete request -> manifest in ledger -> index updated by streaming consumer -> Query Gate filters sample queries (synthetic load)
Chaos test: simulate duplicate manifests and manifesto races to validate idempotency and compactor behavior
Performance test: measure added p95 latency on Console queries with Query Gate cold/warm caches
Compliance test: generate attestation bundle and have Compliance team (Laila Gupta) verify signature and completeness
comments: 2026-02-22 — Spike complete: verified a manifest-first approach avoids race conditions we observed in the prior tombstone-only flow. Prototype writes to S3 and we can observe consumer-driven index updates within ~12s on dev cluster. — Marco Chen

2026-02-28 — Security review (Laila Gupta): requested KMS envelope encryption for manifests and HSM-backed signing for attestation bundles. Also asked for retention policy for signing keys. Added IKMS task to deps. — Aisha Verma

2026-03-04 — PM feedback (Jordan Rivera): customers require downloadable attestation for legal hold; propose adding CSV export option for compaction receipts. Also requested UX copy changes for Console deletion modal. — Marco Chen

2026-03-07 — Performance concern from infra (Diego Alvarez): Query Gate adds ~6ms p95 when cold; suggested LRU + local replica cache and async prefetch for known dashboards. Implementing cache in next spike. — Marco Chen

2026-03-10 — Design decision: implement Query Gate + Compactor hybrid. Query Gate provides near-term guarantees for interactive workloads; Compactor does physical removal after safety window. Filing follow-up tasks to tune index granularity and compaction windows. — Aisha Verma
